interpretation: For this fixed-input unidbg profile, the varying pre-block buffer byte has a positive data dependency on the address returned by calloc(1,95). At +0x16aa48, wrapper +0x268504 targets the loaded libc calloc symbol at +0x1baa0. Its 32 live code bytes have the same fingerprint as the pinned sdk23/lib64/libc.so resource and dynsym entry in unidbg-android-0.9.9.jar. At the matching dispatcher-SP return, X0 equals the descriptor word at +0x18 and the 95-byte allocation is zero-filled. That returned pointer equals the pre-block buffer address. The LOAD64 at bytecode +0xa0614 reads the exact descriptor return slot; its result equals the pointer, then AND16 at +0xa064c feeds the left OR64 operand at +0xa0654. The other OR operand is stable within each run. The reconstructed expression from the observed callback pointer, mask and other operand equals the architectural OR result; its low byte equals buffer[0], written at +0xa0658. Within each of two independent four-call runs, all six pointer comparisons are A-B-A-B, as are the masked varying operand and pre-block byte. This explains the observed fixed emulator profile dependency without proving why the allocator reuses those addresses or how Android behaves. No guest intervention was performed.
